Bitcoin is trading essentially flat near $60,100, hovering just above a critical support level and near its 52-week low, as the market attempts to stabilize following a brutal multi-day selloff driven by a hotter-than-expected May PCE inflation print of 4.1% — a three-year high — that reignited Federal Reserve hawkishness and crushed rate-cut hopes. Bitcoin is declining, trading near 21-month lows after hotter-than-expected US PCE inflation data rattled risk assets, with May PCE coming in at 4.1% — a three-year high — triggering a Nasdaq 100 sell-off and intensifying fears of Fed rate hikes under Chair Kevin Warsh. The decline is being driven by a record 13-day streak of U.S. spot Bitcoin ETF outflows exceeding $3 billion, Strategy's first Bitcoin sale in nearly four years (which broke a key market narrative), over $1 billion in leveraged long liquidations, escalating U.S.-Iran geopolitical tensions dampening risk appetite, and a strong jobs report that pushed markets to price in near-zero odds of Fed rate cuts in 2026.
